Lina Gomez: Quick update — launching a 2-month pilot for two related items: Short-Trip PTO Declaration and an Emergency PTO Top-up pilot. TL;DR: 
- Emergency PTO Top-up: one-time advance of up to 3 days for unexpected caregiver/medical emergencies (manager-approved). Reconciled on next payroll.
- Short-Trip PTO Declaration: simplified lightweight declaration for same-country trips under 72 hours so you don’t need full travel preapproval.
Full policy + FAQ here: https://redwood.company/hr/short-trip-pto-pilot (please read before submitting). :spiral_notepad:

Alex Chen: thanks — quick q: does the top-up change accruals or affect payroll deductions?

Lina Gomez: Good question. No change to accrual rules. The top-up is an advance from your future PTO balance and is reconciled on the next payroll cycle if/when accruals catch up. It is not taxable income. Managers sign off on the advance.

Priya Patel: who’s eligible for the pilot? Contractors? part-timers?

Lina Gomez: Eligibility: full-time employees and contractors on engagements >6 months. Part-time / hourly employees — case-by-case; reach out to people-ops@redwood.company. We’ll capture eligibility in the form.

Sam Rivera: clarification — does Short-Trip Declaration cover international short trips (e.g., quick UK trip from EU office)?

Lina Gomez: No — international travel still requires the standard travel preapproval and safety checklist. Short-Trip Declaration is for same-country travel only (or travel within the same legal entity). If in doubt, default to the full preapproval.

People Ops Bot: New doc uploaded to handbook: /handbook/people-ops/short-trip-pto-declaration.md — includes the form link, manager checklist, and retroactive request flow.

Alex Chen: If an emergency already happened, can we ask for the top-up retroactively?

Lina Gomez: Yes — managers can submit retrospective requests within 10 business days of the event. Use the form and put `RETRO-TOPUP` in the "notes" field so payroll flags it. Retro requests require manager sign-off + brief explanation.

Priya Patel: Will this be visible in Console/HR dashboard or is it only between manager & People Ops?

Lina Gomez: It will appear as a flagged PTO transaction in the HR dashboard for payroll/reconciliation and for People Ops reporting. No passport/visa info will be stored as part of the declaration.

Sam Rivera: Do managers need training to approve these?

Lina Gomez: We’ve got a short 15-minute async training in LMS for managers — covers eligibility, evidence, and how to use the form. Completion required for people approving more than 3 requests in the pilot. Link in the doc.

Priya Patel: Sounds helpful, thanks! :thumbsup:

Lina Gomez: Pilot window: May 1 — June 30. We’ll collect metrics (approval times, number of top-ups, retro requests) and a short user survey mid-pilot. If you run into edge cases, DM me or ping people-ops. Thanks all — appreciate quick read and spread the word to your teams. :heart:
